name: Internal Consistency and Self-Feedback in Large Language Models: A Survey
authors: Xun Liang, Shichao Song, Zifan Zheng, et al. (lead affiliation: School of Information, Renmin University of China; LLM Center, Institute for Advanced Algorithms Research (IAAR), Shanghai; corresponding author Zhiyu Li)
venue: arXiv preprint (cs.CL); not formally peer-reviewed at time of survey (v1 Jul 2024, v3 Sep 2024)
reflection_type: calibration/probing (unified 'Internal Consistency' lens spanning latent/decoding/response layers) — survey covers all reflection types: verbal-self-critique (Verbal Critiquing, Self-Refine/Reflexion), learned-critic-model, multi-agent-debate, contrastive-decoding probing, and uncertainty/confidence/consistency estimation. Not a single method; it abstracts them under Self-Evaluation + Self-Update.
feedback_source: Predominantly self-generated (internal consistency signals from sampling across latent/decoding/response layers; e.g. Self-Consistency majority voting, verbal self-critique, hidden-state/attention-head probing). The survey explicitly notes 'generalized Self-Feedback' can also use other models (SelfEvaluate_N) or external tools (SelfEvaluate_tool), so external-tool and inter-model feedback are also surveyed.
iteration_structure: Surveys the full spectrum: single-shot (Self-Consistency sampling), iterative-refine (Self-Refine, Reflexion, Self-Debug), tree/search (Tree-of-Thoughts, Graph-of-Thoughts, MCTS-based self-improvement), and multi-agent collaboration/debate. Framework itself is layer-agnostic (Self-Evaluate -> Self-Update loop).
reflection_object: Survey scope spans multiple objects of reflection/modification. Self-Update can target (a) the output/response content (iterative response refinement), (b) the reasoning chain (Reasoning Topologically: CoT/ToT/GoT), (c) decoding distribution (truthful/contrastive decoding), (d) latent-layer activations (activating truthfulness, attention-head steering), and (e) the model's own weights (fine-tuning on self-selected/self-corrected data, e.g. Self-Improve, LEMA, Mistake Tuning). Unifying lens: 'internal consistency' across latent, decoding, and response layers.
requires_training: Surveys both training-free and training-based methods: none/in-context (Self-Consistency, Self-Refine, decoding-time methods) and SFT (self-generated data fine-tuning, e.g. Self-Improve, LEMA, Mistake Tuning) plus preference/RL approaches (DPO/RLHF discussed under Preference Learning). Survey itself requires no training (n/a as a method).
reward_or_critic_model: Surveys the range: self-as-judge (verbal self-critique, sampling/voting as scalar signal), trained reward/value functions (value function for best-selection), separate models (NLI models, other LLMs in debate), and internal-state probes (latent consistency as an implicit critic). Central abstraction: feedback signal f from SelfEvaluate.
distillation_target: Surveys multiple distillation/persistence targets: prompt/response (in-context refinement), model-weights (fine-tuning on self-generated/self-corrected reasoning data — Self-Improve, LEMA, Mistake Tuning, Self-improvement via MCTS data synthesis), and student-model distillation (Eq. 8, SelfUpdate_N updating a separate student / LLM-based knowledge distillation in Section VII). No dedicated episodic-memory/skill-library focus (agentic memory is largely out of scope).
emergent_vs_engineered: Primarily covers prompt/scaffold-engineered reflective behaviors (Self-Refine, Reflexion, Multi-Agent Debate, decoding-time interventions). Predates the o1/R1 RL-emergent 'aha' reflection wave (survey v3 is Sep 2024), though its 'Reasoning Paradox' (latent vs explicit reasoning) and future-directions anticipate native/latent reflection. So: engineered-leaning, with forward-looking discussion toward emergent latent reasoning.
memory_type: n/a (survey; not an agent with memory). The lens is internal consistency (latent/decoding/response sampling), not episodic memory. Methods reviewed mostly use short-term/scratchpad-style iterative context; long-term/skill-library agentic memory is largely outside the survey's scope (agent memory listed among out-of-scope/related areas).
memory_persistence: n/a — surveyed methods operate mostly within-episode (single-task refinement); cross-task persistence appears only via weight updates (fine-tuning on self-generated data). Survey itself has no memory.
memory_curation_mechanism: n/a (survey does not propose a memory-curation scheme). For weight-update methods reviewed, the analog of curation is data selection/filtering (e.g. majority-vote best-response selection, GPT-4-annotated corrected rationales in LEMA) used to build fine-tuning datasets.
error_localization_granularity: Survey spans granularities: holistic/outcome-level (Self-Consistency answer voting), response-level (iterative response refinement, hallucination alleviation), step-level (reasoning-chain critique, topological reasoning over CoT/ToT/GoT nodes), token/decoding-level (truthful/contrastive decoding), latent-level (attention-head / hidden-state consistency), and agent-level (multi-agent collaboration/debate). Explicitly framed by the latent/decoding/response 'Hourglass' layering.
intra_task_vs_inter_task: Covers both. Intra-task: refine within one task (Self-Refine, iterative response refinement, decoding-time correction). Inter-task: transfer via weight updates (Self-Improve/LEMA/Mistake Tuning fine-tune the model so improvement persists across tasks). Emphasis is more on intra-task consistency mining than agentic cross-task experience transfer.
failure_recovery_vs_avoidance: Mix of post-hoc-revision (iterative refinement of an already-produced response/CoT) and avoidance via learning (fine-tuning to avoid prior mistakes, e.g. 'Learning from mistakes' / Mistake Tuning). Mid-trajectory recovery is less central (predates Agent-R-style in-flight correction). Decoding-time methods act in-flight to steer toward truthful tokens.
task_domains: QA/reasoning (math, knowledge, logic), free-form generation / hallucination mitigation, code generation, dialogue, and general alignment/preference learning. Two flagship task buckets in the survey: Reasoning Elevation (QA) and Hallucination Alleviation (open-ended generation); plus 'Others' (preference learning, knowledge distillation, data augmentation).
benchmarks: Common evaluation benchmarks tabulated (Table VI): C-Eval, MMLU, BBH, ARC, WiC, HumanEval, MATH, GSM8K. Other tasks referenced in critique/discussion include TruthfulQA, Game-of-24, Graph Coloring, and planning tasks. Survey also catalogs meta-evaluation methods/benchmarks for Self-Feedback components.
headline_result: No single headline number (it is a survey, not an empirical method). Its core qualitative 'result'/claim: Self-Feedback reliably improves internal consistency ('Does Self-Feedback improve internal consistency? Yes'), but whether internal consistency equals correctness 'cannot be directly concluded' — captured by the 'Consistency Is (Almost) Correctness' hypothesis. It organizes 100+ 'Self-*' works under the unified Self-Evaluation + Self-Update framework across latent/decoding/response layers.
baselines: n/a (survey). Positions itself against prior surveys that 'predominantly focus on categorization' and against fragmented/biased treatments of 'Does self-correction work' (e.g. it argues Huang et al. and Kamoi et al. give either limited-perspective or overly-complex answers). Provides a unified internal-consistency-based alternative framing.
gains_vs_baseline: n/a (no empirical delta; survey). Conceptual contributions over prior surveys: (1) unified Self-Feedback framework (Self-Evaluation + Self-Update) instead of pure categorization; (2) layer-based 'Hourglass Evolution of Internal Consistency' (latent -> decoding -> response); (3) a more 'insightful' affirmative-but-qualified answer to 'Does Self-Feedback Really Work?'; (4) novel hypotheses: 'Consistency Is (Almost) Correctness' and 'The Paradox of Latent and Explicit Reasoning'.
compute_cost_profile: n/a as a survey; but it discusses cost as a critique axis — e.g. it relays Huang et al.'s point that Multi-Agent Debate is 'resource-heavy' and inferior to (cheaper) Self-Consistency, and that sampling/iterative refinement methods multiply inference calls. No quantified token/FLOP multipliers of its own.
known_limitations: Survey-stated limitations of the field it reviews: (1) self-correction often depends on external/oracle feedback to actually improve (Huang et al. [87], Kamoi et al. [21]); (2) models are better at generating than verifying answers (SELF-[IN]CORRECT, Jiang et al. [137]); (3) self-verifiers produce many false positives (Stechly/Valmeekam on Graph Coloring & planning); (4) self-refinement can amplify self-bias (cites 'Pride and Prejudice'); (5) internal consistency does not guarantee correctness (vagueness/hallucination inherent to probabilistic LMs). Survey-specific: largely pre-o1/R1 reasoning-model era; agentic long-term memory mostly out of scope.
oracle_or_external_feedback_dependency: Explicitly the discriminating variable in the survey's critique synthesis. It distinguishes intrinsic-only / self-verify methods from those needing external-tool/verifier or oracle-label/ground-truth. Key relayed finding: Reflexion-style refinement relying on external truth is 'impractical' when no oracle exists; self-correction works best on decomposable or verifiable tasks (where verification is easier than generation, e.g. Game-of-24), and is unreliable on QA without external signals.
self_correction_efficacy: task-dependent / requires-oracle. Survey's nuanced conclusion: Self-Feedback DOES improve internal consistency (net-positive on consistency), but improvement in CORRECTNESS is not guaranteed and is task-dependent — feasible for decomposable/verifiable tasks, unreliable (sometimes net-negative/degrading) for intrinsic self-correction on open QA without external/oracle feedback (consistent with Huang et al. 'LLMs cannot self-correct reasoning yet').
calibration_effect: mixed / partly negative. The survey notes models show 'overconfidence without understanding their capability limits' and relays self-bias amplification under self-refinement; internal-consistency signals can serve self-evaluation/calibration (cites Calibrating Reasoning with Internal Consistency) but consistency is not equal to correctness. Net: calibration via self-feedback is promising but not reliably positive (mixed).
failure_attribution_capability: classifies-failure-mode (taxonomy). As a survey it organizes the field into a taxonomy (4 tasks: Consistency Signal Acquisition, Reasoning Elevation, Hallucination Alleviation, Others; lines of work in Table IV) and catalogs causes of low internal consistency (inadequate latent reasoning, hallucination snowball effect, stochastic-parrot hypothesis). It does not attribute responsibility to specific agents/steps in a trace.
failure_mode_addressed: Targets/exposes: reasoning deficiencies and hallucinations (the two core problems), inconsistent responses to identical queries, overconfidence/miscalibration, superficial or ineffective self-reflection/self-correction (relayed critiques), self-bias amplification in self-refinement, and the latent-vs-explicit reasoning tension ('Reasoning Paradox'). Related to MAST modes such as superficial self-reflection and overconfidence, though the survey predates and does not use the MAST taxonomy.
dataset_or_benchmark_released: No new dataset/benchmark proposed. Releases an open-source resource hub (paper list, framework figures, the Hourglass/Internal-Consistency experiment code) at https://github.com/IAAR-Shanghai/ICSFSurvey. Tabulates existing evaluation benchmarks (Table VI: C-Eval, MMLU, BBH, ARC, WiC, HumanEval, MATH, GSM8K) and meta-evaluation methods rather than releasing one.
builds_on: Synthesizes and builds on the 'Self-*' literature: Self-Consistency (Wang et al.), Self-Refine (Madaan et al.), Reflexion (Shinn et al.), Self-Improve (Huang et al.), Tree-of-Thoughts (Yao et al.), Graph-of-Thoughts, Quiet-STaR/STaR, Self-Debug, LEMA (Learning from Mistakes), Mistake Tuning, SelfCheckGPT, Multi-Agent Debate, contrastive/context-aware decoding (DoLa, CAD), and the critique works Huang et al. ('LLMs Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet'), Kamoi et al. (self-correction survey), and SELF-[IN]CORRECT (Jiang et al.).
extended_by_or_inspired: Cited by ~53 follow-up works (Semantic Scholar, Jun 2026), including: 'LLMs Know More Than They Show: On the Intrinsic Representation of LLM Hallucinations' (Orgad et al., ICLR 2025), 'Scalable Best-of-N Selection via Self-Certainty' (Kang/Zhao/Song 2025), 'DSVD: Dynamic Self-Verify Decoding' (EMNLP 2025), 'Dynamic Attention-Guided Context Decoding (DAGCD)' (ACL 2025), 'Latent Debate' (2025), 'Alleviating Hallucinations with Scepticism Modeling' (2024), 'Calibrating Reasoning with Internal Consistency' (NeurIPS 2024), and several hallucination/cognition surveys (e.g. Loki's Dance of Illusions).
citation_count: ~53 (Semantic Scholar, Jun 2026; cross-checked: Semantic Scholar search snippet ~50, paperswithcode ~52)
reasoning_model_native: Mostly no / forward-looking. Survey v3 (Sep 2024) predates wide o1/R1 adoption and focuses on engineered Self-* methods, but its 'Internal Consistency' framing across latent/decoding/response layers and 'The Paradox of Latent and Explicit Reasoning' directly motivate study of native latent reasoning in reasoning models; it anticipates rather than targets o1/R1-style built-in reflection.
on_policy_distillation_link: Indirect. Surveys self-distillation / self-improvement where a model fine-tunes on its own (often self-selected via majority-vote/MCTS, hence on-policy-flavored) generations (Self-Improve, LEMA, Mistake Tuning) and student-model updates via SelfUpdate_N (Eq. 8). This is conceptually adjacent to on-policy distillation / self-training, though the survey does not use that terminology or analyze it as OPD.
sample_efficiency: n/a (survey; no single trials-to-gain figure). It does relay efficiency-relevant critiques (e.g. Multi-Agent Debate is resource-heavy vs Self-Consistency; sampling/iterative methods multiply inference calls), and its 'Reasoning Paradox' frames efficient use of reasoning resources as an open problem.
